summary: Missoula County, MT L-4 cab on the Lolo National Forest at 7,780 ft: built 1947, destroyed 1963, listed as a ground site. No source describes the site today.

facts.design: L-4 cab (firelookout.com); ground site per the state list
facts.status_note: firelookout.com says destroyed in 1963; cause not given

evidence.supports: built 1947 as an L-4 cab; destroyed 1963
location 25 miles northwest of Seeley Lake
listed as a ground-type site, status gone, Missoula County
L-4 cab was by far the most popular live-in lookout
evidence.quote: L-4 cab was by far the most popular live-in lookout.

evidence.supports: L-4 cab is a 14x14 foot wood frame cab that could sit on the ground or atop a tower
evidence.quote: It was a 14x14' wood frame cab, windows all around and either sitting on the ground or atop pole or timber towers up to 100 feet high.

sources.title: Hemlock Point
sources.publisher: Montana Forest Lookouts (Rex's Fire Lookout Page)

notes_for_editor: Only firelookout.com gives the dates and elevation; the Forest Lookouts page adds only the Lolo National Forest and a township-section reference. The L-4 design comes from a Sanders County article about a different county, used only as general background. No access, staffing or fire information found. Access key omitted. Search found no Hemlock Point-specific article.
